front: In AWS Lambda, the maximum timeout of a function is {{c1::900 seconds}}.
In AWS Lambda, the default timeout of a new function is {{c1::3 seconds}}.
In AWS Lambda, a function's memory can be set from 128 MB to {{c1::10,240 MB}}.
extra: You change it in [1-MB increments](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-memory-range), and CPU follows it.

front: In AWS Lambda, the default concurrent executions quota per account per Region is {{c1::1,000}}.
extra: [Tens of thousands](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-concurrent-executions-default) is how high a quota increase can take it.

front: In AWS Lambda, after a failed asynchronous invocation, Lambda by default tries {{c1::two more times}}.
extra: The wait grows to [two minutes between the second and third attempts](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-default-two-retries).

front: In AWS Lambda, a synchronous request payload can be at most {{c1::6 MB}}.
extra: The response of a synchronous call has the same limit.

front: In AWS Lambda, a container image function can be up to {{c1::10 GB}} uncompressed.
extra: The size includes all layers of the image.

front: In AWS Lambda, the /tmp storage of a function can be set from 512 MB to {{c1::10,240 MB}}.
